_provenance: Fitted 2026-07-09 from guided captures (tools/calibration/), then feel-tuned on hardware: RX trims ~0.85x (pitch oversensitive), RY- trim 1.5x (roll right slow) with compensated cross row, RX->TY cross kept below fitted strength (forward pushes carry incidental pitch), curves rebalanced translation-flat/rotation-steep for coordinated orbiting. 2026-11-17: translation trims/dead zones and all curves retuned to match a real SpaceNavigator (see the dated _notes).
_notes: Trims were hand-adjusted after fitting: RX (pitch) ~0.85x, RY- (roll right) 1.5x. When a source axis's trim changes after fitting, its CROSS rows must be rescaled by old_trim/new_trim so the correction stays constant in absolute terms.

RX source rows rescaled for the RX trim change (0.870->0.740 pos, 1.121->0.950 neg), EXCEPT RX->TY, which deliberately keeps the pre-rescale values: forward pushes carry incidental pitch and the full-strength correction ate enough forward pan to feel slow.
cross_neg RY row scaled 1/1.5 to offset the RY- trim boost.

Only rotation->translation and translation->TZ cross terms above 0.15 are corrected. TZ drifts most, hence the widest dead zone. Translation curves flatter than rotation so coordinated orbit (strafe while rotating) stays balanced.

2026-11-17 translation gain: raw-HID captures (2 runs each) vs a real SpaceNavigator showed firm pushes peaking at 78-217 (X), 84-139 (Y), 93 pull-up / 278-333 push-down, where the SpaceNavigator saturates at 350 on every axis. Translation trims raised so a firm push reaches ~1.15x full scale before the curve (TX +1.56/-2.37x, TY +2.52/-2.05x, TZ +1.18/-2.10x); TX/TY cross source rows rescaled by old/new trim; X/Y dead zones raised to 65/85 to stay 1.25x above the boosted rest noise (measured from debug telemetry). Rotation and the twist->roll bleed are unchanged (needs recalibration).

2026-11-17 curves flattened (translation 1.35/1.5 -> 1.2/1.35, rotation 2.0-2.1 -> 1.5-1.6): gentle-rotation captures on the real SpaceNavigator hold 65-300 with a near-linear low end, where the steeper curves gave a few percent; Devon found fine changes, rotation most, sluggish. Rotation stays a little steeper than translation for orbit balance.
